Blocked by G7 on the documented pybind11 native path for this card. LAST GATE OUTPUT (backend fake, 2026-11-17, `python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/robots/mrpt__mrpt --backend fake --verbose`): G1 pass, G2 pass, G3 pass, G4 pass, G5 pass, G6 pass, G7 fail, G8 warn, G9 skip. G7 errors: (1) G7.NOT_AN_ENTRY_SYMBOL: native pybind:modules/mrpt_hwdrivers/python_bindings/mrpt_hwdrivers_py.cpp#mrpt.hwdrivers.CTaoboticsIMU is not one of the card's entry_symbols ['mrpt.hwdrivers:CTaoboticsIMU']; (2) G7.NATIVE_NOT_FOUND: modules/mrpt_hwdrivers/python_bindings/mrpt_hwdrivers_py.cpp has no pybind11 class_ declaration of mrpt::hwdrivers::CTaoboticsIMU at the pinned commit. G8 warns SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE (the read-only sensor declares no limit on an actuating capability); G9 did not run. The digest above is the report's report_digest (the CLI printed no separate digest line).

MINIMAL REPRO: the exact gate command is the repro; the two findings are the SDK's own G7. They are not a package-side defect: the binding declares CTaoboticsIMU as a py::class_ expression with no variable name and chains .def calls (modules/mrpt_hwdrivers/python_bindings/mrpt_hwdrivers_py.cpp:121-129), and MHS/sdk/docs/source-selectors.md:76-81 states that 'a declaration without a variable (members bound by chained .def calls) is reported, not read'. The card's own symbol cannot replace the selector either: mrpt.hwdrivers:CTaoboticsIMU is a runtime re-export from the compiled extension (modules/mrpt_hwdrivers/python/mrpt/hwdrivers/__init__.py:20-26), the only Python file with the class text is the _bindings.pyi (not a .py file the loader may read), and class_surface on the card's module follows the import only into .py files, so it reports that CTaoboticsIMU is not defined in __init__.py.

LATENT THIRD ISSUE: even with the chained declaration parsed, the pybind surface reader reads only the selected class's own block, not its CGenericSensor base. initialize, doProcess, getObservations and getState are bound on CGenericSensor (modules/mrpt_hwdrivers/python_bindings/mrpt_hwdrivers_py.cpp:65-89), which the real runtime inherits; the fake's use of those upstream members would then be reported as G7.NOT_UPSTREAM. The documented pybind reader does not follow C++ base classes (MHS/sdk/docs/source-selectors.md:80-83).

WHY NO PACKAGE FIX: the upstream clone is read-only, task.json cannot be edited, and the SDK cannot be edited. A pass needs both an orchestrator card correction (the entry_symbols value changed to the pybind selector, or an entry check that accepts it) and an SDK change (read a variable-less py::class_ declaration and its CGenericSensor base, or G7 exempting inherited bound members). I did not work around either by editing the SDK, the card or the clone.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's helper is PythonObjectDriver, but the package is a direct Driver over the pybind class. The capability read needs per-observation extraction (obs.get(TIMUDataIndex...)) and conversion of the MRPT Clock time_point to RFC 3339; the PythonObjectDriver result map can only map paths of one native return, so it cannot express the observation filter and conversion. The primary interface (one cap.sensing.imu.v1 read of the hfi-a9 observation) is preserved.

WHAT THE PACKAGE DOES: one cap.sensing.imu.v1 action reads doProcess()/getObservations() until a complete hfi-a9 observation arrives (2 s, the class's 2000 ms max_duration_ms), returns linear_acceleration and angular_velocity in body or world frame, orientation when present, and sampled_at. Risk R0 (passive sensor; no actuation). The safe_state says there is no safe state to command because the class has no stop, enable, motion or reset method (CTaoboticsIMU.h:90-152; CGenericSensor.h:97-108). There are no Limits and no operator overlay. The fake is an F0 analytic stand-in with placeholder values and no recording; it preserves setSerialPort/setSerialBaudRate/initialize/doProcess/getObservations. The hfi-b6 parser stores no measurement (CTaoboticsIMU.cpp:144-246), so those observations are skipped and the read times out rather than reporting zeros. Hardware: native.py requires port= and imports a built MRPT Python binding at the pin; it was never run, no IMU or serial device was attached, and reviewed_by stays null. Nothing here is a hardware run or an MHS-Device level.

NOT COVERED: sensor pose and label in the capability output (they are native configuration), the magnetometer entries, the hfi-b6 parser, the raw 35-entry array, and the serial framing itself. The fake has no serial parsing and its values/timestamp are placeholders, not facts.
